title: The Bridge (by Austin Baraki & Jordan Feigenbaum ft Alan Thrall) Program review
summary: He reviews Barbell Medicine's The Bridge, an RPE-based 8-week novice-to-intermediate powerlifting program. He praises its exercise choices and GPP work for strength, but would never recommend it for hypertrophy because it leaves out many muscles and movement patterns.
claims: The Bridge is a powerlifting program built around squat, bench and deadlift, and it makes no hypertrophy claims
Many people run powerlifting programs when what they really want is to get bigger
Alan Thrall was one of the first channels he followed and taught him a lot about proper form and technique
Designing an RPE-based program to move lifters from beginner to intermediate is a smart idea

Novice programs are high frequency, high intensity, low volume while intermediate programs are lower frequency, high volume, moderate-high intensity; the jump from 45-minute to 90-minute sessions burns people out or bores them
Needing a bridge exposes a flaw in novice programs: they should already introduce volume gradually, even if it keeps people novices a bit longer
The program runs 8 weeks of low, medium and high stress, manipulating intensity through RPE, reps and sets, then restarts with new numbers
A belt adds weight on the bar for most people, so powerlifters should use one
Squats as single sets of 5 at RPE 6, 7 and 8 work as warm-ups leading to a top set and as quality volume, which beats 3 sets at the same intensity
He prefers 6-10 reps on close grip bench, but bench is the compound where he accepts low reps most, especially close grip: it is shoulder-safe and if the triceps fail the bar just comes down
A new variation should start easy; close grip bench at 4 reps to RPE 9 is not traumatising
He prefers rack pulls from below the kneecap; the higher the block the less specific, and above the knee it is no longer a hip hinge and does not carry over to the deadlift
Dead-stop rack pulls for 7 reps at RPE 8 are a good range and let you reset and focus on form each rep
Getting more hip hinge work than knee flexion work in a day is good for knee health
Pause squats after the belted squat day are fine because they tax the knees and lower back less; 4 reps at RPE 9 for 12 relevant reps
The pause squat is the best paused lift: it builds confidence out of the hole and teaches you to stay with the lift without panicking
15 total reps of overhead press at RPE 8 is on the low side given it is the only vertical press in the program
Do not go below 6 reps on barbell rows or you will jerk the bar instead of using the back; rows need hamstring, lower back and glute rigidity, so avoid very high intensities
Rather than doubling the top set of barbell rows he would have preferred vertical pulls in the program
GPP builds work capacity and recovery; many people fail intermediate programs because their muscular or cardiovascular endurance cannot keep up
Placing GPP after the two squat days sends blood to the legs without being too intense before deadlift day
Pulls from the floor are essential in every style; many natural bodybuilders skip them and that is why their backs are underdeveloped
One set of 5 deadlifts is a great range when deadlifting once a week with rack pulls to complement; the deadlift can be strengthened without much volume
Paused bench is the second best paused lift, a lifesaver for people with shoulder pain and good for grooving the lift
About 27 weekly reps of horizontal pressing with no push-ups is on the low side
Tempo squats with a 3-0-3 tempo artificially raise difficulty, so RPE 8 on them is not a real RPE 8
The squat is not an easy lift unless you have very short legs; this much squatting may cause knee pain
Back squatting three times a week may be difficult to sustain
For hypertrophy he would never recommend it: long head triceps, traps, neck, rear and medial delts, calves, mid traps, lats and biceps get little or no work
Powerlifting trains the prime movers of the lifts, which is why it ignores muscles like calves and rear delts
It lacks a stretch-focused hip hinge for the hamstrings and any vertical pull; pull-ups are key for building lats
Running such a program for looks gives massive quads, a decent chest and thick posterior chain but little else; he went through that himself
There is no room to modify it toward hypertrophy; it should be reserved for people making powerlifting their main pursuit
Most novice programs already funnel people into powerlifting under the guise of building a base
Running one or two mesocycles of it to raise compound strength, then using that strength to push tonnage on a bodybuilding program, is a good use
A bodybuilding program progresses strength more slowly because effort is spread over more exercises and muscles, but it develops every body part
exercises: below the knee, dead stop, 7 reps RPE 8
carries over to deadlift if block is low
lower reps turn it into jerking
